nodes.label: Connecting Postgres (and Other Adapters) Guide
nodes.rationale: Documents the ports-and-adapters (hexagonal) design of the booking system: every external dependency sits behind an interface, and swapping an adapter means writing one class and changing one line in container.ts.

nodes.label: BookingRepository (port)
nodes.rationale: Interface hiding the concrete storage adapter from use cases/Server Actions/components. Postgres implementation must guarantee createIfSlotFree/rescheduleIfSlotFree atomicity, unlike the single-threaded in-memory dev adapter.

nodes.label: CalendarSyncService (future port)
nodes.rationale: Not built: two-way calendar sync needs a registered OAuth app (Google Calendar API / Microsoft Graph), a client secret and consent screen, and per-client refresh-token storage (which itself requires the Postgres swap first) plus a live public deployment. Additive later: a port alongside the existing ones, called from createBooking/cancelBooking/rescheduleBooking the same way NotificationService is today.

nodes.label: container.ts (composition root)
nodes.rationale: Single composition root wiring concrete adapters to ports; no use case, Server Action, or component ever imports a concrete adapter directly.

nodes.label: InMemoryBookingRepository (dev adapter)
nodes.rationale: Checks-then-inserts synchronously; safe only because JS is single-threaded per request. Not safe for Postgres without a SERIALIZABLE transaction or a DB-level EXCLUDE constraint.

nodes.label: ConsoleNotificationService (dev adapter)
nodes.rationale: Logs instead of sending; recommended production swap is Resend for first-class Next.js support, simple API, generous free tier.

nodes.label: InMemoryRateLimiter
nodes.rationale: Only shares state within one Node process; fine for a single long-running server but breaks once deployed across multiple serverless instances, since each instance gets its own memory (the '5 attempts per 15 minutes' limit becomes per-instance). Needs a Redis-backed swap (e.g. Upstash) at scale.

nodes.label: emailComposer.ts
nodes.rationale: Every email's actual content (subject/html/text/attachments) is already fully composed here; a NotificationService adapter only has to transport it.

nodes.label: Postgres EXCLUDE Constraint (btree_gist) Design
nodes.rationale: Recommended over a SERIALIZABLE transaction: an EXCLUDE constraint using btree_gist over (solicitor_slug, tstzrange(slot_start_utc, slot_end_utc)) makes double-booking impossible even under concurrent requests, a guarantee an application-level check alone can't provide. rescheduleIfSlotFree relies on the same constraint by catching the violation error on UPDATE.

nodes.label: Vercel Cron (/vercel.json, hourly)
nodes.rationale: CRON_SECRET set in deployment env vars lets Vercel Cron authenticate automatically; any other scheduler (GitHub Actions cron, traditional crontab with curl -H Authorization Bearer) works identically.

nodes.label: createReview (future use case)
nodes.rationale: Would mirror createBooking's shape and be gated behind the same SpamGuard port the booking form already uses, so no new spam-protection code is needed.

nodes.label: GooglePlacesReviewRepository (hypothetical future adapter)
nodes.rationale: The current Google Reviews section renders seed data filtered to source:'google' — not a live Google Places API integration (no API key configured). Going live requires calling the Places API place/details endpoint server-side and caching the response, since Google's terms cap polling frequency.

nodes.label: Template Folder Overview
